unsupported_assumptions: The draft's 'no retry path' framing is accurate for the supplied source; no separate retry/backoff mechanism exists, so 'retries' reduce to repeated drain() calls — this is a boundary, not a defect.
The scenario's 'drained twice' outcome is stipulated, not observed; the assessment correctly limits itself to static reading.

anchors.explanation: preference() is the withdrawal entrypoint; on ('insights','off') it cancels queued 'report' jobs scoped to the withdrawing owner's cases only.
POST /preference dispatches purpose/value to store.preference, so on and off share the same route.
Single toggle form per purpose; 'Switch off' shown when enabled via the same /preference action — symmetric withdrawal control.
NOTICE discloses optional separate consent, ease of switching off, and future-only effect.
notice() renders NOTICE to the user before choices are made.
enabled() reads the latest choice per owner/purpose, making the gate owner-scoped.
drain() selects only state='queued' jobs, so cancelled reports are not re-selected on a second drain.
Report branch requires enabled(owner,'insights'); withdrawn consent blocks generation even if a job remained queued.
Job state persisted after processing; cancelled jobs are not re-run by subsequent drains.
